output.question: What class action lawsuits has Synchrony Bank faced?
output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, the sources reviewed identify putative class actions against Synchrony Bank involving CareCredit interest rates (S.G. v. Synchrony Bank, filed August 19, 2024), alleged post-service-member interest-rate increases and fees (Taylor et al. v. Synchrony Bank et al., filed June 4, 2024), automated debt-collection calls under the TCPA (including Campbell v. Synchrony Bank, Mott v. Synchrony Bank, and Rajput v. Synchrony Bank), and allegedly misleading collection communications under the FDCPA (Central Credit Services, LLC and Synchrony Bank, filed July 18, 2017). The reviewed sources also list proposed class claims involving PayPal Credit/Synchrony promotional-purchase account handling, but they do not provide enough opened primary material here to verify a case name or outcome. The CareCredit case was still being treated as a putative class action in a January 27, 2026 court recommendation, which recommended arbitration rather than a class proceeding; the reviewed materials do not establish final outcomes for every other matter.

key_facts.fact: S.G. v. Synchrony Bank (No. 2:24-cv-05788) was filed August 19, 2024 as a putative class action alleging that CareCredit charged interest rates exceeding applicable New York usury limits; a January 27, 2026 recommendation addressed Synchrony's motion to compel arbitration.

Taylor et al. v. Synchrony Bank et al. (No. 5:24-cv-00313) was filed June 4, 2024 as a proposed class action alleging that Synchrony raised interest rates and fees on service members' outstanding balances after active duty, contrary to SCRA-related protections and its own military-benefits program.

Campbell v. Synchrony Bank (No. 1:17-cv-00080) was commenced January 25, 2017 as a putative class action alleging automated calls to a wireless number; the court's August 11, 2017 order stayed discovery in the TCPA case.

Mott v. Synchrony Bank (No. 8:18cv275) was filed February 2, 2018 as a proposed TCPA class action alleging automated, unsolicited debt-collection calls to a cellphone concerning a debt the plaintiff said she did not owe.
Rajput v. Synchrony Bank f/k/a GE Capital Retail Bank (No. 3:15-cv-01079) was filed June 1, 2015 and alleged repeated TCPA violations involving calls to the plaintiff's cellular telephone.

Central Credit Services, LLC and Synchrony Bank (No. 2:17-cv-00991) was filed July 18, 2017 as a proposed class action alleging FDCPA violations and conflicting or misleading collection notices about payment deadlines, default, and the amount due.

The Synchrony Bank category page also lists a March 17, 2020 proposed class action alleging that PayPal Credit and Synchrony Bank misled an account holder about Promotional Purchases terms and failed to properly credit a return.

A separate 2014 federal enforcement settlement involving GE Capital Retail Bank, then known as Synchrony Bank, was not a private class action: DOJ and CFPB alleged national-origin discrimination in two credit-card debt-repayment programs and announced $169 million in relief for approximately 108,000 borrowers.

A proposed class action lawsuit alleges Synchrony Financial and subsidiary Synchrony Bank have unfairly penalized military service members by unlawfully increasing interest rates and fees on their outstanding credit card balances when they leave active duty.
This matter was commenced on January 25, 2017, as a putative class action alleging ... Synchrony made automated telephone calls to the wireless telephone number.

Central Credit Services, LLC and Synchrony Bank are the defendants in a proposed class action filed in Wisconsin over alleged violations of federal debt collection laws.
Presently before the Court in this putative class action alleging violations of [law] ... is Defendant Synchrony Bank’s ... motion to compel arbitration.

passages.quote: The settlement resolves claims by the department and the CFPB that GE Capital violated the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) by excluding borrowers who indicated that they preferred communications to be in Spanish or had a mailing address in Puerto Rico from two credit card debt-repayment programs.

caveats: This is a source-based list of matters identified in the pages opened, not a certified complete nationwide docket history.
The allegations in complaints and legal-news summaries are not findings of liability.
The reviewed materials do not verify final dispositions for Campbell, Mott, Rajput, Central Credit Services, Taylor, or the PayPal Credit matters.
In re Synchrony Financial Securities Litigation was omitted from the main list because the opened settlement order names Synchrony Financial, not Synchrony Bank; the query specifies the bank itself.
The 2014 DOJ/CFPB matter is included only as context because it was a government enforcement settlement, not a private class action.
